about.text:
Hi, I'm Kevin Ding, a Computer Engineering student at the University of British Columbia with interests in machine learning, robotics, and computer systems. I am proficient in Python, C++, C, Java, and PyTorch.

I currently contribute to research on reducing latency in world-action models, and my previous research focused on machine learning-based operating-system prefetching at UBC. I also lead the Telemetry team at UBC Supermileage, where I develop embedded firmware and vehicle telemetry systems, including C++ firmware and custom PCBs.

Previously, I worked as a Software Engineer at OSI Maritime Systems, building internal tools for engineering workflows and requirements management. I also worked as a Computer Vision Engineer Intern at SNIBE, building a real-time Python/OpenCV actuator monitoring pipeline.

Outside of engineering, I enjoy basketball, skiing, and swimming. I keep a small LEGO collection, and I enjoy playing Minecraft.

education.degree: Bachelor of Applied Science in Computer Engineering
highlights: Academics: 90% Grade percentage | Trek Excellence Scholarship (Top 5%) | Dean's List, All Terms

experience.title: Software Engineer Co-op
description: Built a full-stack AI assistant enabling engineers to query requirements, traceability, and test cases in Perforce Helix ALM, integrating React/TypeScript, FastAPI, Gemma 4 served with vLLM, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools.
Automated an 8+ hour requirements review workflow by building a Python document comparison pipeline combining exact, fuzzy, and LLM-based matching to detect changes across document revisions.
Cleared a 1,000+ hour engineering backlog by automating the migration of hundreds of engineering documents into Helix ALM using Python and REST APIs.

experience.title: Computer Vision Engineer Intern
description: Built a real-time Python/OpenCV actuator monitoring pipeline processing video at 30 FPS, tracking colored markers to automatically detect stalls and jitter hours before manual inspection.
Extracted actuator trajectories using HSV segmentation and contour centroids, then applied cross-correlation and FFT analysis to detect deviations from expected periodic motion.

researchExperience.title: Undergraduate ML Research Assistant
description: Developed machine learning-based operating system prefetching models that outperformed Leap on 3 of 4 complex workloads, improving prediction accuracy by 50% on average.
Implemented LSTM and attention-based models in PyTorch with autoregressive and direct multi-step prediction, benchmarking prediction accuracy and p50/p99 inference latency.
Built data pipelines processing hundreds of millions of page-fault records across seven workloads for distributed training and evaluation on Compute Canada GPU clusters.

researchExperience.title: Undergraduate Robotics AI Research Assistant
description: Researching techniques for reducing inference latency in world-action models to improve real-time policy execution.
Reproducing and benchmarking robot-learning policies, including ACT, Diffusion Policy, and π0, on RoboTwin to evaluate task success rate and inference latency.

designTeamExperience.title: Vehicle Telemetry Firmware Lead
description: Led development of a vehicle telemetry system over LTE to Google Cloud and Grafana; served as Telemetry Race Engineer at the 2026 Shell Eco-marathon, contributing to a top-9 finish in the Urban Vehicle Concept category.
Developed C++ firmware for a Particle Boron MCU and an STM32 CAN bridge in FreeRTOS to acquire and process telemetry from fuel-cell, ECU, and GPS modules over UART, CAN, and I2C.
Designed and brought up a custom 4-layer PCB in KiCad, including schematic design, power distribution, grounding, and routing of sensitive IMU signals.
Reduced BigQuery costs by 50% by redesigning telemetry payloads, partitioning tables, and optimizing SQL queries.

designTeamExperience.title: Electrical Division Member
description: Implemented embedded C++ drivers and control firmware for a dynamometer system, including PWM-based control of a hysteresis brake and integration with custom electronics for vehicle testing.
Designed a 2-layer PCB in KiCad for the dynamometer’s control electronics, contributing to schematic design, component placement, and board routing.

projects.name: Socratic AI
description: Built a full-stack TypeScript/Next.js tutoring platform integrating Gemini to guide students with Socratic questions and summarize learning gaps for instructors.
Implemented authentication and role-based access using PostgreSQL row-level security to isolate school data, with prompt-injection filtering to protect LLM interactions.
Built the chat backend with Next.js server actions, configurable AI settings, and Redis rate limiting to control request volume and prevent abuse.

projects.name: OS/161 Kernel
description: Extended the OS/161 kernel in C by implementing a first-fit physical memory allocator, multi-level page tables, and TLB fault handling to support virtual memory and address translation.

Built Unix-style process and file management, including fork(), execv(), and waitpid(), per-process file descriptor tables, and synchronization primitives using locks, semaphores, and condition variables.
Developed a Unix-style shell with process spawning, I/O redirection, pipelines, and signal handling for process control.

projects.name: Study Sphere
description: Built a JavaFX desktop application that aggregates real-time study-room availability across multiple UBC campus booking web portals, allowing students to filter and find open spaces from a single app interface.
Engineered an asynchronous Python backend using asyncio and Playwright to scrape multiple booking systems concurrently, reducing availability refresh time to around 5 seconds across 100+ rooms.

projects.name: LLM Fine-Tuning for Spam Detection
description: Fine-tuned a decoder-only transformer for spam detection, comparing zero-shot, prompting, and supervised fine-tuning approaches using token-level log-probabilities for classification.
Achieved 95% test accuracy and placed 3rd of 107 teams in a Kaggle competition using class-weighted loss and posterior calibration to address class imbalance.

projects.name: CNN from Scratch
description: Implemented a convolutional neural network (CNN) from scratch in NumPy with vectorized multi-channel convolution, max pooling, dropout, dense layers, and backpropagation.
Achieved 98% MNIST test accuracy and verified my implementation against PyTorch using gradient checks and comparing training/validation curves.

projects.name: RISC-V Processor
description: Designed a 16-bit RISC-V CPU in SystemVerilog with a 5-stage pipeline (Fetch, Decode, Execute, Memory, Writeback), implementing a custom ALU, control unit, and hazard detection logic for control flow correctness.
Verified RTL correctness through ModelSim simulation and synthesized the design onto a DE1-SoC FPGA using Quartus, meeting timing constraints for deployment.

projects.name: WikiMediator Server
description: Built a thread-safe Wikipedia mediator service in Java that handled concurrent client-server requests, supported AES-encrypted communication and token-based authentication, and processed structured queries.
Designed and implemented a custom cache with LRU eviction and expiration policies, using JWiki, Gson, and ANTLR to improve Wikipedia retrieval, JSON handling, and query parsing performance.
